Send a file How it works

One file per invite. No account needed.

When to use PeerDrop

  • Send a video

    Share the original video with a friend when it’s too big to attach to a message.

  • Hand off a project

    Send a presentation or a project ZIP to a teammate while you’re both online.

  • Share a photo album

    Put a set of photos in one ZIP and send it to a friend or family member.

FAQ

Do both people need to be online?

Yes. Keep both browser tabs open until the transfer finishes. The receiver can then select Save file.

Do I need an account?

You can send or receive a file without signing up. Select Send a file to start, or open the invite you received.

How long does an invite link last?

An unused invite expires after 10 minutes by default. If it expires, ask the sender for a fresh link.

Can I share the same link with more than one person?

Each invite is for one recipient and one file. Create a fresh link for each person and send it privately.

How big can my file be?

PeerDrop has no file-size limit by default. The recipient needs enough free space for the transfer and the saved copy. If a limit applies, you’ll see it when you choose a file.

Can I send more than one file?

Each link sends one file. Send files separately, or put them in a ZIP and send it as one file.

What if I receive an unexpected invite?

You’ll see the file’s name and size before accepting. If you weren’t expecting it, select Decline.

Can either person cancel a transfer?

Yes. Either person can select Cancel transfer while it’s active. The recipient can save the file once it arrives in full.

What if the transfer stops?

Check that both devices are online. Ask the sender for a new link, then keep both tabs open while you try again.

Where does my file go after I save it?

Select Save file, then check your browser’s downloads or the folder you picked. Save it before closing the transfer tab.
